clue.text: Favourites backed to get very short trip?

indicators.note: something backed is moved backwards, so the word for favourites is read from its end

blocks.note: pets are favourites, as in a teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Backing the favourites at the races in hope of a quick little outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A single pace is the briefest possible journey on foot, so it works as a very small trip.

clue.text: Ward's disadvantage?

blocks.note: surface reading: some setback suffered by a person named Ward, or by a hospital ward
setter's reading: the name Ward written back to front gives DRAW, so the word read in reverse is its own description

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the trick: WARD backwards is DRAW, and the answer literally says draw is ward back to front, while also meaning a disadvantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a snag or downside, the standard synonym for a disadvantage or handicap.

clue.text: Sappers, and what they may make to reduce costs

blocks.note: sappers are military engineers, the Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE
sappers dig ditches in the field

explanation.surface: Army engineers and their excavations being cited in a discussion about cutting a budget.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps whose soldiers are nicknamed sappers.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrench is to cut back spending, economising when money becomes tight in business or government.

clue.text: Unknown individual in area

blocks.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknown quantities
a single individual is one

explanation.surface: A mysterious stranger lurking somewhere in the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is a region or district marked off for some purpose, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Nervous of danger, years after conflict

indicators.note: after puts the short abbreviation behind the conflict word in the finished answer

blocks.note: a war is an armed conflict
Y is the standard abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: Someone left jumpy about danger for a long time after fighting in a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wary means being cautious and watchful, alert to possible harm or risk.

clue.text: Look wretched after flying finally round the world

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it
after places the look-and-wretched pieces behind the single letter taken

blocks.note: the last letter of flying
lo is an old word for look or behold
bally is a dated British mild curse meaning wretched or damned

explanation.surface: A traveller looking worn out at the end of a long round-the-world flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Bally is an old British euphemism for bloody, used as a mild intensifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done globally happens all over the planet, everywhere on the earth, worldwide.

clue.text: Every route mentioned, without exception

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the phrase is judged by its sound

blocks.note: every route is all the ways one could go

explanation.surface: Insisting that every single road gets named, with none left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Always means at every time, invariably, which is what happens without any exception.

clue.text: Country losing a game, sort of blue

indicators.note: losing tells us the country drops the single letter named next

blocks.note: a country of South Asia
the letter to be removed
go is the East Asian board game

explanation.surface: A nation's sports team losing a match, leaving fans a bit blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep violet-blue dye and colour, one of the shades of blue.

clue.text: I ask chef to prepare food

indicators.note: preparing a dish means mixing and working the ingredients, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner requesting that the cook make them something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishcake is a patty of flaked fish and mashed potato, fried, so a kind of food.

clue.text: Branch added to fine, growing business perhaps

indicators.note: added to means the branch word is attached behind the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an arm is a branch, as of an organisation

explanation.surface: A new branch office bolted on to a thriving, expanding company.
explanation.walkthrough: Growing business looks like a booming company, but it is literally a business that grows crops.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm grows crops or livestock for a living, so it is a business that grows things.

clue.text: One that secures a level

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who ties things fast
second meaning: a rank or layer in a stacked arrangement

explanation.walkthrough: Read as tie-er, the first sense is a person who ties; the usual word is a row or layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows or layers placed one above another, like a storey.

clue.text: Advise little boy to be relaxed

blocks.note: to inform is to tell or advise
Al is a short form of a boy's name such as Alan

explanation.surface: Telling a young lad that he should calm down and loosen up.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means casual and unceremonious, free of stiffness, so easygoing or laid-back.

clue.text: Nervous girl speaking Native American language

indicators.note: speaking means we go by how the words sound when said out loud

blocks.note: a nervous girl is a shy Ann

explanation.surface: A timid young woman talking in an indigenous American tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheyenne is the Algonquian tongue spoken by the Cheyenne people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: To make a fuss?

definitions.note: with the article, a to-do is a fuss

blocks.note: taken as written
to do is to make, as in do a drawing

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether to kick up a stink about something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one infinitive phrase; split it and the first two words build the answer while the last two define it.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion or flap, an excited bother over something, which is a fuss.

clue.text: The end of a little piggy?

definitions.text: The end of a little piggy?

blocks.clueFragment: The end of a little piggy?
blocks.note: surface reading: the tail or snout of a piglet
setter's reading: in the nursery rhyme This Little Piggy each piggy is a toe, and its tip is covered by a horny plate

explanation.walkthrough: This Little Piggy is a children's rhyme counted on the toes, so each little piggy is a toe.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard plate at the tip of a toe sits at the very end of what the rhyme calls a little piggy.

clue.text: Fun time politicians organised

blocks.note: first meaning: a festive social gathering
second meaning: an organised body of politicians

explanation.surface: Politicians arranging a jolly evening out for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a celebration with guests and a formal political grouping like Labour.

clue.text: Teacher's not quite finished

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: done means finished

explanation.surface: A teacher who hasn't yet wrapped up the lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a college teacher or tutor at a university, a British academic term.

clue.text: Olympian falling in pit? Oh dear!

indicators.note: falling in tumbles things about, so the following letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete at the Games tumbling into a hole, to cries of dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: Olympian suggests a sports star but means one of the gods of Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite, goddess of love, was one of the twelve gods dwelling on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: A way to keep up excited feeling, seeing bird

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means higher in the column, so the feeling sits on top of the rest

blocks.note: a buzz is a thrill of excitement
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's tip for staying thrilled on a twitching trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzard is a large broad-winged hawk, a bird of prey common in Britain.

clue.text: Some American alone in Panama, for example

indicators.note: some means only a part of the words that follow is wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A lone American traveller in Panama, perhaps a tourist.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama looks like the country, but it is the waterway cut across it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panama is the famous ship waterway linking Atlantic and Pacific, an example of the class.

clue.text: Good European position for development

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
E is the abbreviation for European
a station is a post or position

explanation.surface: A fine job on the Continent that would be great for one's career growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestation is the growing of young in the womb, and by extension the maturing of an idea.

clue.text: Wrong about husband - one seldom seen in pubs these days?

definitions.text: one seldom seen in pubs these days?

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for wrong wraps the single letter

blocks.note: gone astray means gone wrong
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A mistake about someone's husband, a man who rarely goes drinking any more.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hints at a rare pubgoer; since UK pubs banned smoking, places to stub out cigarettes are rarely seen there.
explanation.definitionFit: Since smoking was banned indoors in British pubs, dishes for cigarette ash have mostly vanished from them.

clue.text: Flowers for Judy

definitions.note: the answer is singular: a ring of flowers

blocks.note: first meaning: a wreath of flowers
second meaning: surname of the star of The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: Someone buying a bouquet for a woman called Judy.
explanation.definitionFit: A garland is a wreath of blooms, and Judy Garland was the actress who played Dorothy.

clue.text: National flag over hospital

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the flag word above the abbreviation

blocks.note: a flag is a type of iris plant, the yellow flag
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A country's banner flying above a hospital building.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag looks like a banner, but here it is a plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the adjective for Ireland, describing a citizen or thing belonging to that nation.

clue.text: Strike, capturing rook, for winning position

indicators.note: capturing means taking hold of, so the strike word encloses the chess piece letter

blocks.note: to fist is to strike with the hand
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess move: taking the opponent's rook to secure a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming first means taking top place in a race or contest, the position of the winner.

clue.text: Unlikely response to sentry's challenge?

blocks.note: surface reading: an odd reply given to a guard
setter's reading: the sentry asks Friend or ...?, and an enemy would hardly admit to the second option

explanation.walkthrough: The classic challenge is Halt, friend or foe?; nobody approaching a guard would answer with the hostile choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe is an enemy, the second alternative offered in the guard's traditional challenge.
